summary: Very hard if you need to read or send mail for users outside your organisation: almost every useful Gmail scope (read, modify, compose, metadata, full access) is restricted, which means brand verification (an automated check that usually takes minutes, or about 2-3 business days if it goes to manual review), restricted scope verification that Google says can take several weeks, and a security assessment by a Google-approved third party (CASA) that must be repeated at least every 12 months. Sending only (gmail.send) is a sensitive scope, which still needs verification but no security assessment. Creating the Google Cloud project and OAuth client takes about an hour and works at once in Testing mode for up to 100 test users, but their tokens expire after 7 days. Two ways around the long path: use Composio's managed Gmail app (users see Composio's app on the consent screen instead of yours, so you skip registering your own; fine for prototypes and internal tools), or, if all your users are in your own Google Workspace organisation, set the consent screen to Internal, which does not need verification.

difficulty.reason: Reading, modifying or drafting mail needs restricted scopes. Restricted scopes need brand verification, restricted scope verification (several weeks) and, because a server such as Composio's stores or transmits the data, a yearly third-party security assessment. Internal apps in your own Workspace org, test builds, and personal-use apps with a few known users skip this.

evidence.label: INFERRED
evidence.note: The scope tiers come from the Gmail scopes page; the verification and annual assessment rules come from Google's restricted scope verification page. The overall rating is ours, based on those two pages.

time.detail: Hands-on: 1-2 hours to get a working Testing-mode app; roughly 2-5 working days more to prepare verification (privacy policy, domain verification, demo video, scope justifications) plus the security assessment work. Approval wait: Brand verification: the automated check usually takes minutes, and a manual review typically 2-3 business days; restricted scope verification several weeks (Google's unverified-apps page says it may take several months), with the security assessment running alongside.

evidence.label: INFERRED
evidence.note: Google states the automated brand check typically takes a few minutes and a manual review usually 2-3 business days and restricted scope verification 'can potentially take several weeks'; the unverified apps page says verification 'might require several months' depending on the data. The day ranges and hands-on hours are our estimate from those statements and the list of things to prepare; Google gives no exact figure.

requirements.name: Google Cloud project and Google Account
requirements.detail: The OAuth client, consent screen branding, scopes and verification requests all live in one Google Cloud project. Google recommends separate projects for testing and production.

requirements.name: Public home page on a domain you own
requirements.detail: Needed for verification. It must be publicly reachable without login, clearly about the app, and describe what the app does. A Play Store or Facebook page does not count.

requirements.name: Privacy policy on the same domain
requirements.detail: Must be linked on the consent screen, hosted on the same domain as the home page, disclose how the app accesses, uses, stores and shares Google user data, and comply with the Google API Services User Data Policy and its Limited Use rules.

requirements.name: Domain ownership verified in Google Search Console
requirements.detail: Verify the authorized domains in Search Console using an account that is Owner or Editor on the Cloud project. Google will not approve verification until this is done.

requirements.name: Demo video (unlisted YouTube)
requirements.detail: Needed for sensitive or restricted scope verification. It must show the consent flow in English, the app name on the consent screen, the client ID in the address bar, and each requested scope in use. Task automation platforms must show how workflows are built and which way data flows.

requirements.name: Third-party security assessment (CASA)
requirements.detail: Required when the app uses restricted scopes and can access the data from or through a server. With Composio the tokens and API calls go through Composio's servers, so in practice a production Gmail app reading mail should expect this. Google's Trust and Safety team contacts you when it is time to start, and the app is assigned assurance level AL1 or AL2 based on user count, scopes and other signals. It must be revalidated every year (at least every 12 months after the Letter of Assessment).

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: The rule is sourced. Applying it to a Composio-based app is our reading, since Composio stores and uses the tokens server side.

requirements.name: Google Workspace organisation (only for the Internal shortcut)
requirements.detail: If every user is in your own Workspace or Cloud Identity organisation, an org-owned project with the Internal user type needs no verification. An admin may still need to approve the app.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.labels
scopes.purpose: See and edit email labels. Listed with the add-on scopes gmail.addons.current.action.compose and gmail.addons.current.message.action as non-sensitive.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Google's verification help says non-sensitive only apps do not have to be verified, but need brand verification to show a name and logo. The Gmail scopes page words this as 'basic OAuth App Verification'.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send
scopes.purpose: Send email on the user's behalf. Sensitive, not restricted.

scopes.name: gmail.addons.current.message.metadata and gmail.addons.current.message.readonly
scopes.purpose: Read message metadata or content while a Workspace add-on is running. Sensitive; only relevant to add-ons.

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify
scopes.purpose: Read, compose and send email; cannot permanently delete (bypassing trash).

scopes.name: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.metadata
scopes.purpose: View message metadata such as labels and headers, not the body.

scopes.name: https://mail.google.com/
scopes.purpose: Full access including immediate permanent delete. Google says request it only if you need to bypass the trash.

scopes.name: gmail.insert, gmail.settings.basic, gmail.settings.sharing
scopes.purpose: Insert mail into the mailbox, change settings and filters, manage delegation. Also restricted; settings.sharing is limited to Workspace service accounts with domain-wide delegation.

steps.title: Decide whether you need your own app yet
steps.action: Check whether Composio's managed Gmail app covers your scopes. If you are prototyping or building an internal tool, stay on managed auth and skip the rest. Switch to your own app when you need your own name on the consent screen, scopes Composio does not request, or your own quota.
steps.expected_result: A clear decision: managed auth for now, or your own Google OAuth app.

steps.title: Pick the narrowest Gmail scopes
steps.action: List the Gmail actions your agent needs and map them to scopes. Prefer gmail.send (sensitive) if you only send mail; anything that reads mail is restricted. Do not request https://mail.google.com/ unless you must delete permanently.
steps.expected_result: A short scope list with a one-line reason for each, ready for the human to review.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.action: Sign in to Google Cloud console, create (or select) a project for production, and enable the Gmail API for it. Add a second Google account as Owner or Editor so verification emails are not missed.
steps.expected_result: A project with the Gmail API enabled.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Google recommends separate test and production projects and extra Owners or Editors for verification emails. The exact console link for enabling the API was not opened by us.

steps.title: Fill in branding
steps.action: On the Branding page enter app name, logo, support email, developer contact, home page, privacy policy and authorized domains. Changes are saved as draft branding.

steps.title: Choose the user type and add test users
steps.action: On the Audience page choose Internal if all users are in your own Workspace organisation; otherwise External, which starts in Testing. In Testing, add up to 100 test users.
steps.expected_result: The app works for listed test users (their authorizations expire after 7 days).

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Google's help page links the user type setting to the Audience page; we did not open the signed-in console to check exact button labels.

steps.title: Declare your Gmail scopes on the Data Access page
steps.action: On the Data Access page use Add or remove scopes to declare every Gmail scope your Composio auth config will request. Google groups them as non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted.
steps.expected_result: The declared scopes match the scopes in your Composio auth config exactly.

steps.title: Create a Web application OAuth client with Composio's redirect URI
steps.action: On the Clients page create an OAuth client of type Web application and add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback as an Authorized redirect URI. Copy the client ID and client secret.
steps.expected_result: A client ID and client secret. The redirect URI matches exactly, so no redirect_uri_mismatch error.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Our probe confirmed the Clients page URL loads (it redirects to sign-in), but creating the client needs a logged-in human.

steps.title: Create a custom auth config in Composio
steps.action: In the Composio dashboard click Create Auth Config, pick Gmail, choose OAuth2, turn on Use your own developer credentials, paste the client ID and secret, set the Redirect URI to the same Composio callback, add your scopes, and create it. Pass the auth config ID in your session's auth_configs.
steps.expected_result: An auth config ID (ac_...) that your sessions use for Gmail instead of the managed app.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Composio notes some toolkit defaults still use the older https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add callback; set the v3 URL explicitly in both places.

steps.title: Test the full connect flow with a test user
steps.action: Connect a test user's Gmail through a Composio Connect Link and run one tool call per scope. Record this flow; it becomes your demo video.
steps.expected_result: The test user sees the consent screen with your app name and the agent can call Gmail.

evidence.label: INFERRED
evidence.note: Practical step we recommend; reusing the test for the demo video follows from Google's video requirements.

steps.title: Prepare the verification material
steps.action: Draft the privacy policy section on Google user data and Limited Use, a justification for each sensitive or restricted scope explaining why narrower scopes are not enough, and the demo video script. If your product is a task automation platform (most agent products are), the video must show how multiple API workflows are created and automated and which directions user data flows. The human reviews, publishes the policy and records the video (unlisted on YouTube).
steps.expected_result: Published privacy policy, verified domain in Search Console, scope justifications, unlisted demo video link.

steps.title: Verify branding, then submit data access for verification
steps.action: On the Branding page click Verify Branding and then Publish branding. Then open the Verification Center, add the demo video link, pick your permitted application type, explain why narrower scopes are not enough, and submit. Watch the developer contact email for follow-ups from Google's Trust and Safety team.
steps.expected_result: Branding published (the automated check usually takes minutes; a manual review typically 2-3 business days); data access request under review.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes)
steps.action: Google's Trust and Safety team contacts you when it is time to start the CASA assessment and assigns assurance level AL1 or AL2. Work with an assessor authorized under the App Defense Alliance CASA framework. Revalidate every year (at least every 12 months after the Letter of Assessment), and again if you add a new restricted scope.
steps.expected_result: A Letter of Assessment; once verification passes, the unverified-app screen and 100-user cap are removed.

review_process.trigger: Any sensitive scope (for example gmail.send) or restricted scope (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.metadata, https://mail.google.com/ and others) used by users outside your organisation. Not needed for Testing mode, personal use, or Internal apps in your own Workspace org.
what_to_submit: Published branding (app name, logo, support email, home page, privacy policy, authorized domains)
Domain ownership verified in Google Search Console
Every scope declared on the Data Access page
Declared scopes with a reason why narrower scopes are not enough
Unlisted YouTube demo video of the consent flow and each scope in use; task automation platforms must also show how multiple API workflows are created and automated
Security assessment (CASA) letter for restricted scopes accessed through a server
review_process.typical_wait: Brand verification: usually minutes (automated) or 2-3 business days (manual review); restricted scope verification several weeks, possibly months, plus the security assessment
common_rejections: Requested scopes in code differ from the scopes declared on the consent screen
Privacy policy does not disclose Google user data use or Limited Use
Home page not public or not clearly about the app
Demo video does not show the consent screen, client ID, or each scope in use
Domain not verified by a project Owner or Editor

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: The rejection list is built from Google's stated requirements, not from a published list of rejection reasons.

blockers.blocker: Restricted scopes need a paid third-party security assessment every year
blockers.how_to_get_past: Use gmail.send only if sending is enough (sensitive, no assessment); keep users inside your own Workspace org with the Internal user type; or stay on Composio's managed Gmail app.

blockers.blocker: Testing mode: at most 100 test users and authorizations expire after 7 days
blockers.how_to_get_past: Publish the app (In production) and complete verification; until then Composio connections will need reconnecting weekly.

blockers.blocker: Unverified app screen and a 100 new-user cap
blockers.how_to_get_past: Finish verification; the warning screen is removed from your client once verified.
blockers.contact: Verification Center in Google Cloud console

blockers.blocker: Changing redirect URIs, app name or scopes after verification can trigger re-verification
blockers.how_to_get_past: Register the Composio callback before you submit and keep the scope list final.

nuances.detail: In Testing mode with an External user type, authorizations and refresh tokens expire after 7 days (except basic profile-only scopes).
Limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per OAuth client ID; a new one silently invalidates the oldest. Repeated reconnects for the same user can kill older connections.

A refresh token with Gmail scopes stops working when the user changes their password. Tokens also die after 6 months unused, on revocation, when a Workspace admin restricts the service, when the user exceeds the maximum number of live refresh tokens for their account, or when a time-based grant expires. In Composio the connection then needs reconnecting.
An org-owned project with the Internal user type serves only your Workspace or Cloud Identity organisation and does not need verification; outside users get an org_internal error.
Google's discovery document lists PKCE methods plain and S256, and the authorize endpoint rejected a fake client ID with invalid_client.
Redirect URIs must use HTTPS (localhost excepted) and match exactly; Composio's v3 callback must be set in both Google and the Composio auth config.
Restricted scope apps must be re-verified and re-assessed at least every 12 months; adding a new restricted scope may need a new assessment.

Limited Use: you may not use Gmail data to create, train or improve AI or machine learning models beyond that user's own personalized model for a user-facing feature. Humans may read the data only with the user's agreement or for security, legal or aggregated internal reasons. State this in your privacy policy and design your agent's logging and memory to match.

unverified: Cost of the CASA security assessment: Google's pages do not state a price.
How long the CASA assessment itself takes.
Exactly which Gmail scopes Composio's managed app requests by default.
Whether Google's 100 new-user cap for unverified apps is the same in every case; Google says quotas may be adjusted per app.

composio_note.detail: Gmail is in Composio's managed OAuth list (snapshot 2026-10-28). With the managed app your users see Composio's app on the consent screen, and Composio maintains the app registration, client credentials and redirect URI. That lets you skip setting up your own Google app while prototyping or for internal tools. You need your own app for your own branding on the consent screen, scopes beyond Composio's defaults, or dedicated quota, and then you inherit the full verification path above. You can mix: your own app for Gmail, managed auth for other toolkits.

evidence.label: SOURCED
evidence.note: Our inference, not stated by Composio: because Google only serves restricted Gmail scopes to the public from a verified app, Composio's managed app must have passed Google verification and CASA, so you do not need to while you use it.
